subject: Urgent remediation request — BrightBridge production impact & contract remedy
messages:
From: Carlos Mendoza <carlos@brightbridge.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Elise Tan <elise@brightbridge.io>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Production impact: elevated latency & errors (BrightBridge)

Priyom —

We had a significant production degradation on BrightBridge this morning between ~10:20–14:35 PDT. Symptoms observed: 95th percentile inference latency spiked from ~420ms to ~2.3s, overall error rate climbed to ~7% (timeouts + 500s), and throughput dropped ~40% on our ingest path. This impacted several customer workflows and caused multiple timeouts in our frontend.

We’ve attached logs and a sample of failing requests (service_logs_20260809.zip). Our contract references an SLA with latency and availability targets; this incident clearly impacted our production SLAs. We need: (1) immediate explanation of root cause, (2) a remediation plan & timeline, and (3) an estimate of contractual remedies/credits you intend to offer for the impacted window.

This is already escalated internally at BrightBridge. Please assign an exec-level contact and confirm next steps within 2 business hours.

—Carlos
Carlos Mendoza
Head of Platform, BrightBridge
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production impact: elevated latency & errors (BrightBridge)

Hi Carlos —

I’m very sorry for the impact this morning. Thank you for the logs; our on-call has the incident and we’ve escalated to engineering and SRE. Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Opened an incident (INC-20260809-BB) and placed a hard priority on reducing error rates and restoring throughput.
- Triggered failover policies to a compatible model variant in us-west-2 to reduce latency while we investigate.
- Captured a pre/post snapshot of the KV cache & batch queue for RCA.

I’ll be your executive contact on this — I’ll coordinate updates and a proposed commercial remedy. Expect an engineering RCA and a remediation timeline within 24 hours. In parallel, I’ve asked Legal/Finance for an initial credit range to share with you for the impacted billing period.

Can you confirm the most critical business windows we should prioritize for mitigation and whether you want us to apply immediate pro-rated credits pending a final postmortem?

—Priyom

On Mon, Aug 9, 2026 at 4:00 PM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> I’ll be your executive contact on this — I’ll coordinate updates and a proposed commercial remedy.

Thanks — quick technical summary from SRE: around 10:15 PDT a maintenance job triggered a GPU driver restart on a subset of nodes serving BB’s model profile in us-west-2. Our fallback path restarted the model processes but we saw a KV-cache invalidation cascade: many requests regenerated KV cache simultaneously causing larger-than-expected load (thundering herd). That pushed worker queue depth up and caused timeouts and elevated latency.

Mitigations applied: rolling restart sequencing to avoid simultaneous cache rebuilds, temporary throttling on background maintenance, and an emergency traffic split to healthy capacity. We believe the fix is a change to sequencing and a cap on concurrent cache rebuilds; we’re testing a patch now and expect to deploy within 36 hours during a controlled maintenance window. Full RCA will include exact node counts and wallclock metrics.

Dev
Dev Patel
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Folks —

Customer is sensitive and this is already an exec-level escalation on their side. Commercial stance: we need to move quickly but also limit unnecessary exposure. Propose the following as an interim offer to Carlos while we finalize RCA and a legal addendum:
- Immediate pro-rated credit of 15% for the impacted billing quantity for August (applied to next invoice), pending final RCA.
- Free one month of dedicated capacity at a 50% discount as a goodwill gesture (to offset perceived reliability risk).

Reasons: shows good faith, helps BrightBridge stabilize, and keeps the deal relationship healthy while legal and engineering finish the details. If engineering metrics indicate a broader impact, we can revisit to a higher credit bracket.

Grace

Carlos / Elise —

Thank you again for the quick flag and for sharing the logs. Summary of what we’re proposing today to close the immediate escalation:
1) Interim commercial remedy: a pro-rated 20% credit on August invoicing tied to the impacted request volume (applied to the next invoice). We’re offering 20% rather than 15% to show good faith while we complete the RCA.
2) Operational remedies: emergency patch to sequencing and cache-rebuild caps (target deployment within 36 hours), plus an offer of one month of dedicated capacity at 50% off to help stabilize production while you migrate if you prefer isolation.
3) Timeline & deliverables: preliminary RCA within 24 hours, full RCA and technical postmortem within 72 hours. Formal remediation addendum (legal) shared via DocuSign for signature; we’ll only apply the credit after signature, unless you request an immediate pro-rated invoice adjustment.
